speaker: Doctor
text: Let me start by understanding your symptoms better. When did your vomiting and chest pain begin, and have you noticed any specific triggers like food or movement?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (spontaneous esophageal rupture). 

I have already assessed the timeline and triggers; the combination of forceful retching after heavy alcohol consumption, followed immediately by severe chest pain and respiratory distress in a middle-aged male, is classic for this life-threatening condition. Immediate surgical consultation and chest imaging are required.
